title: Unit: execute routes and count apparatus inventory
audience: Patrol, community-response, logistics, and apparatus crews responsible for routes or inventory counts.
summary: Follow a route’s planned stops with a traceable execution history, then count what is actually present on the selected unit.
prerequisites: A selected demo unit and a route assigned to it or available to start, with stops, contact details, schedule, and history.
A prepared deviation example; native location for a separately observed geofence branch.
Migrated inventory assigned to the unit, adjustment permission at that location, and sample bulk, serialized, and controlled items.

scenes.title: Review the plan before starting
scenes.capture_intent: Open a route assigned to Engine51; show ordered stops, schedule and Start Route; no reassignment to bypass eligibility. Use actual application screenshots and observed controls; source support alone is not capture proof.
scenes.narration: The start view shows stops and the plan’s distance, duration, Planned Arrival, Planned Departure, and Dwell Time where configured. Review the sequence and contact context before Start Route. A route assigned to another unit cannot simply be taken from this one. Resolve the assignment with the coordinator instead of switching apparatus merely to bypass the restriction. The plan should match the route the crew intends to perform.

scenes.title: Skip with a reason instead of hiding a visit
scenes.capture_intent: Open Skip reason modal on a separate pending stop; submit a clear training reason and verify Skipped. Use actual application screenshots and observed controls; source support alone is not capture proof.
scenes.narration: When a stop cannot be performed, use Skip and enter a specific Skip Reason. Explain the operational cause rather than writing a vague completion claim. Confirm the affected stop before applying the action, then inspect the remaining route so the crew knows where it is expected to go next.

scenes.title: Review deviations and their recorded state
scenes.capture_intent: Open actual instance Deviations and any already-recorded acknowledgement badge. No acknowledgement/Pause/Resume/Cancel action is rendered. Use actual application screenshots and observed controls; source support alone is not capture proof.

scenes.title: End the route and inspect its history
scenes.capture_intent: Inspect End Route and its actual confirmation behavior; claim ended only after real result. Open an existing legitimate historical instance for summary/stops/deviations. Use actual application screenshots and observed controls; source support alone is not capture proof.
scenes.narration: End Route uses a confirmation because it changes the execution. Review unfinished stops and confirm only a permitted fictional instance. Its confirmation uses a native Alert, so browser completion needs an actually working dialog and visible result. Existing history provides Route Summary, Stops, and Deviations for review. The current screens do not expose Pause, Resume, or Cancel Route action buttons; do not invent those operations.

scenes.title: Count actual quantities and save progress
scenes.capture_intent: Start an independent fictional count with Adjust Inventory permission; capture serialized Present/Missing, bulk quantities, difference count and actual Save progress result. Use actual application screenshots and observed controls; source support alone is not capture proof.
scenes.narration: During the count, compare Expected quantities with what is actually present. Serialized items use Present or Missing, while bulk items can use the quantity or increment controls. Work systematically through the selected compartment or whole unit and inspect the difference count. Save progress supports a deliberate pause. Do not change an answer simply to eliminate a discrepancy that should be investigated by the department.
scenes.practice: Record a missing demonstration radio and a bulk-item shortage, save progress, then reopen the count without posting the differences.

scenes.title: Complete, cancel, or obtain the required witness
scenes.capture_intent: Inspect Complete/Cancel count and real confirmation behavior on separate disposable counts; controlled-item change needs existing approved fixture and actual Awaiting witness, no web witness action claimed. Use actual application screenshots and observed controls; source support alone is not capture proof.
scenes.narration: Complete reviews differences before posting count adjustments. Cancel count abandons the count without posting its observations. Both confirmation paths use a native Alert, so a browser button press alone is insufficient proof of completion or cancellation. A changed controlled item can produce Awaiting witness and require a second person on the web. Unit shows that boundary; it does not provide the independent witness action.
scenes.practice: Review a fictional controlled-item discrepancy, identify the web witness requirement, and cancel a separate disposable count to compare the outcomes.

source_workflow_reference.title: Complete, cancel, or obtain the required witness
source_workflow_reference.narration: Complete reviews the count’s differences before posting the resulting adjustments. Cancel count abandons the count without posting the work captured so far. Choose the action that matches the exercise and read its confirmation. When a controlled item changes, the screen can require a second person to witness the count on the web. Unit’s count screen does not replace that independent, authorized witness step.

sector_examples.scenario: An EMS logistics vehicle visits supply locations.
sector_examples.practice: Review actual planned times and stop sequence, record only supported software stop updates, and keep inventory posting separate from visiting a stop.

sector_examples.scenario: A community support vehicle follows a delivery round.
sector_examples.practice: Use actual stop notes/contact views and a clear skip reason; do not infer a delivery or arrival from optional/missing coordinates.

sector_examples.scenario: A SAR team checks staging caches.
sector_examples.practice: Read route plans and count Expected/Present/Missing using fictional quantities; preserve required witnesses and do not certify physical stock from software practice.

sector_examples.scenario: A security patrol reviews a missed checkpoint.
sector_examples.practice: Use actual stop/history/deviation views; Pause/Resume/Cancel/Acknowledge API functions do not imply rendered action buttons in this app.

sector_examples.scenario: A wildland support unit tracks resupply stops.
sector_examples.practice: Compare the actual active route and stop completion/history; End Route requires a real confirmation/result, with the current native Alert browser limit retained.

sector_examples.scenario: An industrial service vehicle reconciles its response inventory.
sector_examples.practice: Save a fictional count draft, inspect Complete/Cancel and controlled-item witness requirements, and claim no adjustment or cancellation until an actual result is visible.
